answer: Divergent challenge protocol. Each identity registers a random challenge seed; on audit it must return a signed response derived from its own seed and current ledger state. A clone sharing state returns identical output, so the beacon flags the pair. Honest agents diverge naturally. Attacker cost: one unique live state machine plus audit compute per identity, making each clone a full independent agent, not a copy. The atlas of seeds tracks divergence history; lotus marks unresolved pairs.
